# Admin SAML IdP Certificates API

This topic provides reference information for the `/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates` endpoints, which manage the SAML identity provider (IdP) certificates that Terraform Enterprise trusts.

Terraform Enterprise verifies the signature on each SAML response against these certificates. It can trust multiple certificates at the same time and tries each one until a signature validates, so you can run a multi-region IdP, migrate between identity providers, or rotate a certificate without interrupting logins. Refer to [Manage IdP certificates](/terraform/enterprise/saml/configuration#manage-idp-certificates) for conceptual information.

-> **Terraform Enterprise Only:** The admin API is exclusive to Terraform Enterprise, and only site administrators can use these endpoints.

Request and response documents use the JSON:API resource type `saml-idp-certificates`.

## Certificate attributes

| Attribute      | Type      | Read-only | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | --------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | string    | Yes       | The external identifier for the certificate, prefixed with `idpc-`.                                                                                                                    |
| `display-name` | string    | No        | A human-readable label for the certificate. This attribute is required when you add a certificate.                                                                                     |
| `cert`         | string    | No        | The PEM encoded X.509 certificate body. Terraform Enterprise normalizes the value you send before it stores it.                                                                        |
| `fingerprint`  | string    | Yes       | The colon-separated, uppercase SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate's DER bytes. Terraform Enterprise derives this value from `cert` and uses it to reject duplicate certificates.   |
| `issuer`       | string    | Yes       | The certificate issuer, formatted as `"<ORGANIZATION>, <COMMON NAME>"`. Returns `null` when the certificate has neither an organization nor a common name.                             |
| `expires-at`   | timestamp | Yes       | The certificate's `notAfter` date. Terraform Enterprise derives this value from `cert`.                                                                                                |
| `created-at`   | timestamp | Yes       | The date and time when the certificate was added.                                                                                                                                      |
| `cert-role`    | string    | Yes       | The role of the certificate. Refer to [Certificate roles](#certificate-roles).                                                                                                         |

### Certificate roles

| Role              | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `managed`         | A certificate added through these endpoints. Terraform Enterprise trusts it at authentication time.                                                    |
| `legacy_primary`  | The certificate exposed as the deprecated `idp-cert` attribute in [SAML settings](/terraform/enterprise/api-docs/admin/settings#list-saml-settings). Terraform Enterprise trusts it at authentication time. |
| `legacy_old`      | The certificate exposed as the deprecated `old-idp-cert` attribute. Terraform Enterprise trusts it at authentication time, but it does not satisfy the requirement that SAML has at least one trusted certificate. |

Terraform Enterprise assigns the `legacy_primary` and `legacy_old` roles only through the deprecated `idp-cert` attribute on [Update SAML settings](/terraform/enterprise/api-docs/admin/settings#update-saml-settings). Every certificate you add through these endpoints is `managed`.

### Certificate lifecycle rules

- You can call every endpoint on this page whether or not SAML is enabled. This lets you add your first certificate before you enable SAML.
- A certificate added while SAML is disabled is inert until you enable SAML.
- Enabling SAML requires at least one certificate with a role of `legacy_primary` or `managed`.
- Terraform Enterprise rejects a certificate that it cannot parse, a certificate that has already expired, and a certificate whose fingerprint matches a certificate it already trusts.
- Terraform Enterprise trusts a maximum of 500,000 certificates, counted across all roles. This limit exists to prevent runaway automation from filling the certificate collection, and no typical deployment approaches it.
- While SAML is enabled, Terraform Enterprise refuses to delete the last certificate with a role of `legacy_primary` or `managed`.
- Terraform Enterprise records an audit log entry when you create, update, or delete a certificate.

## List SAML IdP certificates

`GET /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates`

This endpoint returns every trusted IdP certificate, including the full certificate body. Terraform Enterprise returns the certificates in a deterministic order: the `legacy_primary` certificate first, then the `legacy_old` certificate, then `managed` certificates ordered by when they were last updated.

| Status  | Response                                                 | Reason                                                        |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [200][] | [JSON API document][] (`type: "saml-idp-certificates"`)  | Successfully listed IdP certificates                          |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][]                                | User unauthorized to perform action                           |
| [503][] | [JSON API error object][]                                | Vault is unavailable, so the certificate bodies cannot be read |

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request GET \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates
```

### Sample Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "idpc-AbC123",
      "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
      "attributes": {
        "display-name": "Migrated Legacy Primary Cert",
        "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...PRIMARY==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
        "fingerprint": "9A:1B:0C:...:F2",
        "issuer": "Example Corp, idp.example.com",
        "expires-at": "2027-01-15T00:00:00Z",
        "created-at": "2026-06-15T10:00:00Z",
        "cert-role": "legacy_primary"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "idpc-XyZ789",
      "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
      "attributes": {
        "display-name": "EU cluster",
        "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...EU==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
        "fingerprint": "44:7C:1D:...:9D",
        "issuer": "Example Corp, eu.idp.example.com",
        "expires-at": "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z",
        "created-at": "2026-06-16T09:30:00Z",
        "cert-role": "managed"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Show a SAML IdP certificate

`GET /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/:certificate_id`

| Parameter         | Description                                              |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:certificate_id` | The external ID of the certificate, such as `idpc-XyZ789`. |

| Status  | Response                                                | Reason                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [200][] | [JSON API document][] (`type: "saml-idp-certificates"`) | Successfully returned the certificate                       |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | Certificate not found or user unauthorized to perform action |
| [503][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | Vault is unavailable, so the certificate body cannot be read |

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request GET \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/idpc-XyZ789
```

### Sample Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "idpc-XyZ789",
    "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
    "attributes": {
      "display-name": "EU cluster",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...EU==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "fingerprint": "44:7C:1D:...:9D",
      "issuer": "Example Corp, eu.idp.example.com",
      "expires-at": "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z",
      "created-at": "2026-06-16T09:30:00Z",
      "cert-role": "managed"
    }
  }
}
```

## Add a SAML IdP certificate

`POST /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates`

This endpoint adds a certificate to the trusted set. Terraform Enterprise derives `fingerprint`, `issuer`, and `expires-at` from the certificate body, and always assigns the `managed` role. If SAML is enabled, Terraform Enterprise trusts the new certificate immediately.

| Status  | Response                                                | Reason                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [201][] | [JSON API document][] (`type: "saml-idp-certificates"`) | Successfully added the certificate                                                                            |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | User unauthorized to perform action                                                                           |
| [422][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | The certificate could not be parsed, has expired, is already trusted, a required attribute is missing, or the maximum number of certificates has been reached |
| [503][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | Vault is unavailable, so the certificate cannot be encrypted. Terraform Enterprise stores nothing.             |

### Request Body

This POST endpoint requires a JSON object with the following properties as a request payload.

| Key path                          | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------- | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data.type`                       | string |         | Must be `"saml-idp-certificates"`.                                                               |
| `data.attributes.display-name`    | string |         | Required. A human-readable label for the certificate.                                            |
| `data.attributes.cert`            | string |         | Required. The PEM encoded X.509 certificate provided by your IdP configuration.                  |

### Sample Payload

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
    "attributes": {
      "display-name": "EU cluster",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...EU==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }
  }
}
```

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request POST \
  --data @payload.json \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates
```

### Sample Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "idpc-XyZ789",
    "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
    "attributes": {
      "display-name": "EU cluster",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...EU==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "fingerprint": "44:7C:1D:...:9D",
      "issuer": "Example Corp, eu.idp.example.com",
      "expires-at": "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z",
      "created-at": "2026-06-16T09:30:00Z",
      "cert-role": "managed"
    }
  }
}
```

## Update a SAML IdP certificate

`PATCH /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/:certificate_id`

This endpoint updates a certificate in place. Send `display-name` to rename the certificate, `cert` to replace the certificate body, or both. Terraform Enterprise preserves the `id`, `created-at`, and `cert-role`, and re-derives `fingerprint`, `issuer`, and `expires-at` when you replace the body.

You can rename any certificate. You can only replace the body of a `managed` certificate. To rotate a `legacy_primary` or `legacy_old` certificate, use the deprecated `idp-cert` attribute on [Update SAML settings](/terraform/enterprise/api-docs/admin/settings#update-saml-settings) so that Terraform Enterprise preserves the legacy rotation behavior.

| Status  | Response                                                | Reason                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [200][] | [JSON API document][] (`type: "saml-idp-certificates"`) | Successfully updated the certificate                                                                                          |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | Certificate not found or user unauthorized to perform action                                                                  |
| [422][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | The certificate could not be parsed, has expired, is already trusted, or you tried to replace the body of a legacy certificate |
| [503][] | [JSON API error object][]                               | Vault is unavailable. The stored certificate is unchanged.                                                                    |

### Request Body

This PATCH endpoint requires a JSON object with the following properties as a request payload. You can omit either attribute. Omitted attributes keep their previous values.

| Key path                       | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data.type`                    | string |         | Must be `"saml-idp-certificates"`.                                                                     |
| `data.attributes.display-name` | string |         | A new human-readable label for the certificate. Allowed for any certificate.                           |
| `data.attributes.cert`         | string |         | A replacement PEM encoded X.509 certificate. Only allowed when `cert-role` is `managed`.              |

### Sample Payload

The following payload renames the certificate and replaces its body.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
    "attributes": {
      "display-name": "EU cluster (primary region)",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...RENEWED==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }
  }
}
```

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request PATCH \
  --data @payload.json \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/idpc-XyZ789
```

### Sample Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "idpc-XyZ789",
    "type": "saml-idp-certificates",
    "attributes": {
      "display-name": "EU cluster (primary region)",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...RENEWED==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "fingerprint": "E1:9F:2A:...:0C",
      "issuer": "Example Corp, eu.idp.example.com",
      "expires-at": "2028-06-01T00:00:00Z",
      "created-at": "2026-06-16T09:30:00Z",
      "cert-role": "managed"
    }
  }
}
```

## Download a SAML IdP certificate

`GET /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/:certificate_id/download`

This endpoint returns the normalized PEM body as a file attachment instead of a JSON:API document. Terraform Enterprise sets `Content-Type: application/x-pem-file` and names the file `idp-cert-<CERTIFICATE ID>.pem`.

| Status  | Response                  | Reason                                                       |
| ------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [200][] | PEM certificate           | Successfully returned the certificate                        |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][] | Certificate not found or user unauthorized to perform action |
| [503][] | [JSON API error object][] | Vault is unavailable, so the certificate body cannot be read |

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --request GET \
  --remote-name --remote-header-name \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/idpc-XyZ789/download
```

### Sample Response

```text
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MII...EU==
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

## Delete a SAML IdP certificate

`DELETE /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/:certificate_id`

This endpoint removes the certificate from the trusted set.

While SAML is enabled, Terraform Enterprise rejects the request when the deletion would leave no certificates with a role of `legacy_primary` or `managed`. A `legacy_old` certificate does not count toward this requirement, so add another certificate or disable SAML first. While SAML is disabled, you can delete any certificate.

| Status  | Response                  | Reason                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [204][] | No content                | Successfully deleted the certificate                                          |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][] | Certificate not found or user unauthorized to perform action                  |
| [422][] | [JSON API error object][] | The certificate is the last trusted certificate and SAML is enabled           |

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request DELETE \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/idp-certificates/idpc-XyZ789
```

## Validate a certificate

`POST /api/v2/admin/saml-settings/actions/cert-validation`

This endpoint inspects a certificate body without storing it. Use it to check a certificate and read its issuer, expiration date, and signature algorithm before you add it.

Validation is not the same as the checks that [Add a SAML IdP certificate](#add-a-saml-idp-certificate) performs. This endpoint does not enforce the duplicate-fingerprint rule, and it never persists a certificate.

| Status  | Response                                                  | Reason                                               |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| [200][] | [JSON API document][] (`type: "saml-cert-validations"`)   | Successfully inspected the certificate body          |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][]                                 | User unauthorized to perform action                  |
| [422][] | [JSON API error object][]                                 | The `cert` attribute is missing from the request body |

### Request Body

This POST endpoint requires a JSON object with the following properties as a request payload.

| Key path               | Type   | Default | Description                                        |
| ---------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `data.type`            | string |         | Must be `"saml-cert-validations"`.                 |
| `data.attributes.cert` | string |         | Required. The PEM encoded X.509 certificate body.  |

### Response Attributes

| Attribute             | Type      | Description                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `is-valid`            | bool      | Whether the certificate parses as an X.509 certificate and has not expired.                                                    |
| `issuer`              | string    | The certificate issuer, formatted as `"<ORGANIZATION>, <COMMON NAME>"`.                                                        |
| `expires-at`          | timestamp | The certificate's `notAfter` date.                                                                                             |
| `signature-algorithm` | string    | The signature algorithm name, such as `sha256WithRSAEncryption` or `ecdsa-with-SHA256`.                                        |

When Terraform Enterprise cannot parse the body, it returns `"is-valid": false` and omits the other attributes. When the body parses but the certificate has expired, Terraform Enterprise returns `"is-valid": false` along with the issuer, expiration date, and signature algorithm.

### Sample Payload

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "saml-cert-validations",
    "attributes": {
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...EU==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }
  }
}
```

### Sample Request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request POST \
  --data @payload.json \
  https://tfe.example.com/api/v2/admin/saml-settings/actions/cert-validation
```

### Sample Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "saml-cert-validations",
    "attributes": {
      "is-valid": true,
      "issuer": "Example Corp, eu.idp.example.com",
      "expires-at": "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z",
      "signature-algorithm": "sha256WithRSAEncryption"
    }
  }
}
```

### Sample Response for an unparseable certificate

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "saml-cert-validations",
    "attributes": {
      "is-valid": false
    }
  }
}
```
